name: Rhode Island
modelName: Income shares, Schedule of Basic Child Support Obligations by combined monthly income (Family Court Administrative Order 2023-02)
incomeDefinition: Combined adjusted gross monthly income of both parents, per the Child Support Guideline Worksheet instructions of Administrative Order 87-02 (carried forward by AO 2023-02). AO 2023-02 also attaches a Gross to Net Conversion Table (2022 federal and state tax rates). Detailed income definitions were not read for this file.

scheduleFacts.columns: combined monthly income, then obligation for 1..6 children
scheduleFacts.lookupRule: Because the tables use $50 increments, the combined adjusted gross income is always rounded upward to the next highest $50 increment, whichever increment it is closer to (AO 2023-02 Report, restating AO 87-02 section IV(B)(6)).
scheduleFacts.note: Rows read by eye on the scanned official PDF (pages 5 and 19); the full table was not certified (see uncertain).

shared.text: The schedule presumes a standard parenting time in which the noncustodial parent has the child at least 20% of overnights; where each parent has at least 49% of the time with one or more children, Administrative Order 2018-01 governs the calculation (AO 2023-02 Report, 'Presumption of Parenting Time'). AO 2018-01 itself was not read.

addOns.childcare: Child care costs are not included in the schedule (AO 2023-02 Report); the worksheet exhibits show child care handled separately.
addOns.healthInsurance: Most health care costs are not in the schedule, but the schedule includes $250 per child per year for ordinary medical expenses (AO 2023-02 Report).
addOns.text: Child care and most health care costs are outside the schedule (AO 2023-02 Report).

lowIncome.rule: The schedule incorporates a self-support reserve updated to the 2022 federal poverty guideline for one person, $1,333 (AO 2023-02 Report). The first schedule row ($1,350) is $50 for 1 to 6 children (read by eye).

statute.cite: R.I. Gen. Laws § 15-5-16.2; Family Court Administrative Order 2023-02

facts.text: The current schedule was adopted by Family Court Administrative Order 2023-02, dated June 22, 2023, effective July 1, 2023, under R.I. Gen. Laws § 15-5-16.2(a).
The schedule is based on the 2021 Betson-Rothbarth measurements (2013-2019 Consumer Expenditure Survey) at August 2022 price levels; the next quadrennial review must start by May 2027.
The 2021-2023 review of 15,350 orders found deviations from the guideline in 1.6% of cases and income imputation in 10.20%.
Combined income is always rounded up to the next $50 schedule line, even when it is closer to the lower line.
